recent_posts.title: Mobile dev Mindtail raises $2M fund for 'AI-powered' games
recent_posts.summary: Istanbul-based mobile game studio Mindtail has closed a $2 million pre-seed funding round led by APY Ventures, with participation from Inveo Ventures and Ak Portföy GSYF. The funding will support an AI-native production model focused on hybrid casual puzzle games, with plans to triple the team and announce a first game soon. The news comes amid broader industry debate over generative AI use in games, with studios like Owlcat, Capcom, Ubisoft, and 11 Bit Studios all drawing attention — sometimes controversially — for their AI-related practices.

recent_posts.title: Why Triple-i Initiative is a 'not-for-profit' event
recent_posts.summary: Evil Empire COO Benjamin Laulan explains how running the Triple-i Initiative as a not-for-profit showcase — charging participating developers ~€14,700 to cover costs only — creates a better marketing event than for-profit alternatives. By maintaining a quality floor and curating a targeted audience rather than maximizing revenue, the 2026 showcase generated over 3 million wishlists with a median of 60,000 per game. Laulan contrasts this with high-cost showcases like The Game Awards, where economics force organizers to accept big publishers and offer free slots to niche darlings, ultimately letting business strategy dictate content. He advises developers to evaluate showcases by audience fit and game performance rather than raw viewership numbers.

recent_posts.title: Atari acquires the rights to five Wizardry titles
recent_posts.summary: Atari has acquired exclusive rights to the first five Wizardry RPG titles and their underlying IP for an undisclosed sum. The deal covers Wizardry I through V, with plans for remasters, collections, console ports, physical releases, and new titles. This continues Atari's strategy of becoming a preservationist publisher under CEO Wade Rosen, following prior acquisitions of Digital Eclipse, Rollercoaster Tycoon 3, and emulation studio Implicit Conversions. Atari previously published a well-received remake of the first Wizardry game through Digital Eclipse.

recent_posts.title: Griffin Gaming Partners launches $100M fund to support indie devs
recent_posts.summary: Griffin Gaming Partners has launched a $100 million Special Opportunities Fund to finance indie game development. Unlike traditional equity investments, the fund provides capital in exchange for a share of a title's revenue, aiming to offer fairer funding to small studios. Hooded Horse CEO Tim Bender will serve as managing director. The fund has already invested in 15 titles, including Darkwood 2, Hellforged, and Menace. The initiative reflects growing recognition of indie games as a fast-growing segment of interactive entertainment and a push for more transparent, developer-friendly financing models.

recent_posts.title: Gearbox Studio Quebec founders start new studio
recent_posts.summary: Former Gearbox Studio Québec co-studio heads Sébastien Caisse and Pierre-André Déry, along with Yanick Piché and Maxime Babin (former Borderlands creative director), have launched Studio Ricochet, an independent game studio based in Québec, Canada. The team also includes veterans from Call of Duty and Assassin's Creed. The studio is focused on original IP for PC and console, currently in early development on a co-op action-adventure game. The founding follows Gearbox's acquisition by Take-Two in 2024, which led to layoffs at both companies.

recent_posts.title: EA boasts record year thanks to Battlefield 6 and EA Sports FC
recent_posts.summary: Electronic Arts reported record net bookings of $8 billion for FY26, a 9% year-over-year increase, driven by the successful launch of Battlefield 6, EA Sports FC 26, and a strong Q4 for Apex Legends. Despite the financial milestone, EA laid off an undisclosed number of Battlefield developers shortly after the game's launch. The company is also navigating a pending acquisition by an investor consortium including Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund PIF, which has drawn concern from US lawmakers and labor unions.

recent_posts.title: EVE Online dev turns independent and rebrands as Fenris Creations
recent_posts.summary: CCP Games, the Icelandic developer behind EVE Online, has been bought back from South Korean publisher Pearl Abyss for $120 million and is rebranding as Fenris Creations. The studio returns to independent operation under its own management and board of directors, with no planned layoffs or restructuring. EVE Online closed 2025 with record revenue in November and over $70 million for the year. Additionally, Google DeepMind has acquired a minority stake in Fenris as part of a research partnership focused on AI topics like long-horizon planning, memory, and continual learning, using an offline version of EVE Online as a research environment.

recent_posts.title: CWA Canada president calls on government to scrutinize EA buyout
recent_posts.summary: CWA Canada president Carmel Smyth has written to Canadian industry minister Mélanie Joly urging government scrutiny of the proposed $55 billion Saudi-led buyout of Electronic Arts. Smyth argues the deal — which would give Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund 93.4% ownership of EA — raises serious national security concerns under the Investment Canada Act, including risks of mass surveillance using Canadian player data, transfer of AI technology to a foreign state, and potential propaganda through EA's gaming platforms. She also warns that the deal's $20 billion debt financing could trigger significant layoffs among EA's thousands of Canadian workers. The concerns echo earlier calls from unionized EA employees and U.S. senators for regulatory review of the acquisition.

recent_posts.title: Xbox appoints new internal leaders and ditches Copilot AI
recent_posts.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the company is winding down Copilot on mobile and halting console development, stating the AI technology does not align with Xbox's direction. Sharma also revealed a leadership overhaul, bringing in executives from CoreAI, GitHub, Meta, and ChatGPT to help Xbox move faster, improve developer tools, and strengthen community connections. Other changes under Sharma include lowering Game Pass prices and retiring the 'This is an Xbox' marketing campaign.

recent_posts.title: Valve to restock Steam Controller after it sells out in a day
recent_posts.summary: Valve's newly released Steam Controller sold out in under an hour after launch, with the company confirming it ran out faster than anticipated. Valve says it is working on a restock and will provide a timeline update soon. Scalpers have already listed the $100 controller on eBay for up to $400.
